tasks.gr12-tricameral-parliament-and-pw-botha-: Topic: Tricameral Parliament and P.W. Botha's reforms. Cover the 1983 constitution, separate chambers for whites, Coloureds, and Indians, exclusion of the African majority, total strategy, limited reforms, continued repression, and why these changes failed to solve apartheid's crisis. Ask Grade 12 learners to analyse reform and continuity.
tasks.gr12-mass-democratic-movement-and-cosatu: Topic: Mass Democratic Movement and COSATU. Cover the UDF, COSATU, civics, youth and church groups, rent and consumer boycotts, stayaways, popular politics, the slogan of making apartheid ungovernable, and links to the ANC tradition. Ask Grade 12 learners to explain mass mobilisation and historical significance.
tasks.gr12-repression-and-states-of-emergency-: Topic: Repression and states of emergency. Cover police and military repression, detention without trial, bannings, censorship, township militarisation, the states of emergency of 1985 and 1986, and why force did not restore apartheid stability. Ask Grade 12 learners to evaluate state power and resistance.
tasks.gr12-sanctions-disinvestment-and-the-roa: Topic: Sanctions, disinvestment, and the road to negotiations. Cover the international anti-apartheid movement, economic sanctions, sports and cultural boycotts, company disinvestment, the impact on the South African economy, and why growing pressure made negotiations more likely by the late 1980s. Ask Grade 12 learners to connect internal and external factors.
